title: Open restriction of the canonical exceptional base-change mate
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of etale Λ-module sheaves. Let g' : X' → X, f' : X' → Y', f : X → Y, g : Y' → Y be a cartesian square sq, with f and f' compactifiable and f' quasi-compact. Let j : U → Y be an open immersion, with cartesian square sqU = (a : V → X, p : V → U, f, j), and assume p compactifiable. Let sqj = (c : U' → U, j' : U' → Y', j, g), sq' = (b : V' → V, p' : V' → U', p, c), and sqV = (a' : V' → X', p', f', j') be cartesian squares with b a = a' g'. Assume p' compactifiable and quasi-compact. For K in D(Y_et,Λ), if the canonical exceptional base-change map beta(p,c) is invertible at Lj* K, then La'* of beta(f,g)_K is invertible. The opens need not be quasi-compact; neither smoothness nor an invertible exponent is assumed.

source.place: Coherences (i) and (iii): restriction of the compactification exchange to a base chart, transposition, and descent.

proof.text: Choose the compactification of f and restrict its proper/open diagram along j. Base change this same diagram along c. Use the graph-factorization construction of the existing unbounded compact-support composition theorem to compare the chosen compactifications without requiring quasi-compactness of f or p. Construct the open-composition comparison j! Fp ≅ Ff a! by proper/open interchange and open-extension composition. Normalize comparison maps between compactifications by their identity on the source open. Inserting the two comparisons into the proper/open exchange diagrams, their cocycle identities cancel the middle comparisons. Proper base-change pasting and degreewise open-extension base change then identify the two compact-support maps on the cube. These constructions use exact extension by zero for the open arrows and do not invoke exceptional base-change maps for those opens.

Take right adjoints of the open-composition comparisons to obtain lambda_f : La* Rf ≅ Rp Lj* and lambda_f' : La'* Rf' ≅ Rp' Lj'*. Let sigma : La'* Lg'* ≅ Lb* La* be induced by b a = a' g', and tau : Lc* Lj* ≅ Lj'* Lg* by sqj. The mate equation defining beta and injectivity of the exceptional-adjunction Hom bijection give La'* beta(f,g)_K followed by lambda_f'(Lg* K) = sigma(Rf K), then Lb*(lambda_f(K)), then beta(p,c)_(Lj* K), then Rp'(tau(K)). To verify this equation, apply Fp' and compose with its counit. Naturality moves the open-composition comparisons through the counit, and the compact-support cube identity from Step 1 makes both expressions inverse exchange followed by the pullback of the original counit.

The hypothesis makes beta(p,c)_(Lj* K) invertible. All remaining factors in the equation of Step 2 are isomorphisms. Functors preserve isomorphisms; cancel lambda_f' to deduce the desired invertibility. This covers empty schemes, the zero ring, identity opens and unbounded K.

proof_origin.place: Coherences (i) and (iii): restriction of the compactification exchange to a base chart, transposition, and descent. The generic compactification calculation is stated without quasi-compactness of the restricting open.

theorem isIso_leftDerivedUpperStar_map_baseChange_of_open_restriction
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X Y X' Y' U V U' V' : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {g' : X' ⟶ X}
    [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification f'] [QuasiCompact f']
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    {j : U ⟶ Y} [IsOpenImmersion j] {a : V ⟶ X} {p : V ⟶ U}
    (sqU : IsPullback a p f j) [HasCompactification p]
    {c : U' ⟶ U} {j' : U' ⟶ Y'} (sqj : IsPullback c j' j g)
    {b : V' ⟶ V} {p' : V' ⟶ U'} (sq' : IsPullback b p' p c)
    [HasCompactification p'] [QuasiCompact p']
    {a' : V' ⟶ X'} (sqV : IsPullback a' p' f' j')
    (w : b ≫ a = a' ≫ g')
    (K : _root_.DerivedCategory (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)))
    (h : IsIso ((rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sq').app
      ((L((j)^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).obj K))) :
    IsIso ((L((a')^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).map
      ((rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sq).app K))
